verdict.rationale: The provided chain shows an administrative-share write of wbemcomn.dll from WKS-4471 to WKS-4472, a new WmiPrvSE instance loading the unsigned file from the wbem directory alongside the signed System32 copy, and WmiPrvSE immediately creating and injecting a remote thread into notepad.exe. This combination is sufficient to treat WKS-4472 as compromised without relying on customer authorization or broader estate context.

observations.desc: On WKS-4472, Security Event 5145 records CORP\j.marsh from 10.24.8.21 requesting WriteData and other write-capable access to C$\Windows\System32\wbem\wbemcomn.dll.
Sysmon recorded System PID 4 creating C:\Windows\System32\wbem\wbemcomn.dll on WKS-4472.
WKS-4471 ran wmic /node:WKS-4472 os get as CORP\j.marsh shortly before the target-side provider activity.
event_refs: Sysmon/1 WKS-4471 2020-10-09 21:34:58.007 Image=WMIC.exe CommandLine=wmic /node:WKS-4472 os get

observations.desc: A new WmiPrvSE.exe PID 8364 on WKS-4472 loaded C:\Windows\System32\wbem\wbemcomn.dll with Signed=false and also loaded the signed Microsoft C:\Windows\System32\wbemcomn.dll.
event_refs: Sysmon/1 WKS-4472 2020-10-09 21:34:58.191 Image=WmiPrvSE.exe PID=8364 User=NT AUTHORITY\NETWORK SERVICE
Sysmon/7 WKS-4472 2020-10-09 21:34:58.195 PID=8364 ImageLoaded=C:\Windows\System32\wbemcomn.dll Signed=true Signature=Microsoft Windows

observations.desc: WmiPrvSE.exe PID 8364 created notepad.exe PID 2580 as NETWORK SERVICE and then created a remote thread in that process; the process-access call trace includes the unsigned wbem-path DLL.
event_refs: Sysmon/1 WKS-4472 2020-10-09 21:34:58.208 ParentImage=WmiPrvSE.exe ParentPID=8364 Image=notepad.exe PID=2580 User=NT AUTHORITY\NETWORK SERVICE
Sysmon/10 WKS-4472 2020-10-09 21:34:58.210 SourcePID=8364 TargetPID=2580 CallTrace includes C:\windows\system32\wbem\wbemcomn.dll

inferences.desc: The file-create and share-audit records are consistent with wbemcomn.dll being staged remotely to WKS-4472 over SMB by CORP\j.marsh from WKS-4471.

The unsigned same-name DLL in WmiPrvSE's wbem directory, contrasted with the signed System32 module, is consistent with DLL search-order hijacking; signature status alone would not establish this mechanism.

The tightly linked remote query, unsigned module load, child creation, DLL-bearing call trace, and remote-thread event demonstrate execution originating from the anomalous provider-host chain and support a malicious compromise determination.

investigations.desc: Acquire and analyze the WKS-4472 wbem-path DLL, validate its hash and signer state, and compare it with the signed System32 module.
Review the available authentication, share-access, and process telemetry for CORP\j.marsh and WKS-4471 around the staging and WMI query.
Collect the WmiPrvSE and notepad process artifacts from WKS-4472 to determine code loaded, thread start context, and subsequent activity.
Ask the customer to validate whether CORP\j.marsh was expected to perform this specific administrative-share write and remote WMI operation.

unknowns.desc: Customer authorization, maintenance, and testing context for CORP\j.marsh is unavailable.
The provenance and full functionality of the unsigned wbem-path DLL are not established by the provided telemetry.
Activity outside WKS-4471 and WKS-4472 or outside the provided time window is unknown.
